A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RegMean++ work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite the expanded content and changed layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging experiments, including vision benchmark accuracies, sequential merging, robustness tests, and layer/component analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the vision experiments and adds language evaluations, internal representation-bias measurements, and computational time and memory results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same activation propagation from previously merged layers, Gram-matrix shrinkage, closed-form merging, and averaging of other weights. The corrected background equations agree with the already-stated pseudocode; the language experiments introduce no documented procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds 11 language benchmarks spanning instruction following, mathematics, coding, safety, and multilingual understanding in French, Spanish, German, and Russian (Sections 4.1 and 5.8; Appendix B.1). The existing vision datasets and test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: v1's sequential-merging comparison includes only RegMean and RegMean++. v2 Figure 5 adds the other ten baselines to the ViT-B/32 sequential comparison, including TSV-M, Iso-C, Iso-CTS, and DOGE AM. Comparator membership in the original vision tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New language experiments introduce Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3.1-8B, an alpha grid search, 256 samples per domain, a 2048-token limit, and task-specific evaluation such as eight-shot GSM8K and coding Pass@1. v2 also adds an eight-task timing/peak-memory benchmark. Existing vision settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds representation-bias analysis across two LayerNorms and GELU throughout all transformer layers for three backbones (Figures 2, 9, and 10), plus computational-efficiency analysis in Appendix D.7. The original final-layer bias, layer/component ablations, and data-characteristic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both disclose five task sequences for sequential merging, five held-out OOD sets, and five class choices for imbalance tests. v2 introduces no new repeated-run disclosure, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: All eleven original tables retain their numerical values. New Table 6 reports RegMean++ versus RegMean averages of 33.0 versus 34.0 for 3B and 45.7 versus 44.8 for 8B. New sequential and representation-bias findings accompany resource measurements, including ViT-L/14 merging times of 171.42 versus 84.09 seconds.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the loss's matrix-product orientation and the shrunken Gram-matrix definition in Section 2. New Appendix A supplies a gradient and convexity derivation of the existing closed-form solution, replacing v1's reliance on an external proof reference.

C1.justification: The central dependency-aware merging and performance claims remain. v2's introduction and conclusion explicitly claim applicability to both vision and language, while removing v1's claim that RegMean++ addresses memory overhead.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises practical limitations around sequential statistic collection and approximately doubled total merging time. It updates the scale boundary to beyond 8B parameters and drops the common-versus-task-specific knowledge caveat. It also develops the nonlinearity-based mechanism explanation and attributes Fisher's imbalance stability to class labels.

D1.justification: v2 adds language dataset/checkpoint links, evaluation details, sampling and sequence-length settings, and resource measurements. It also identifies the four datasets used in corruption testing. However, v1's explicit Euclidean-distance definition of representation bias is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MergeBench, Llama 3, and the language and safety benchmarks, including their underlying datasets. The model-merging related-work discussion and positioning relative to RegMean otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites parts of the motivation and limitations, numbers the experimental subsections, swaps the robustness and OOD subsections, and moves the final-layer bias discussion into the appendix. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to predominantly one column, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v2 adds nonlinear-bias and sequential-comparison figures and language, metric, and resource tables. Existing final-layer radar plots are combined into Figure 13, and several tables gain comparator-category headings.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's explicit lack of billion-parameter evaluations, strengthens the sequential baseline comparison, and quantifies previously undocumented resource costs. The mixed language outcomes in Table 6 clarify applicability limits, while corrected equations and Appendix A improve mathematical consistency. These substantial validation and transparency gains outweigh the smaller reproducibility loss from omitting the bias-distance definition.
